biography: Rafael Cardoso, a name synonymous with flamboyant speed in Brazilian motorsport, hails from the sun-drenched favelas of Rio de Janeiro. Unlike many racers who begin in karts, Rafael's journey started on the treacherous, makeshift tracks of his neighborhood, racing souped-up scooters for scraps and bragging rights. He caught the eye of a local mechanic, 'Zé Electrico,' who saw raw talent and funded his entry into a regional karting series. A defining moment came at the age of 19 during the Brazilian Karting Championship. Despite starting last due to a mechanical failure, Rafael carved his way through the field, executing a daring last-corner overtake to clinch the victory. Currently, he competes with the MetalMoro MRX Duratec Turbo P3 team, aiming to prove his mettle on the international stage. He's known for his aggressive style and never-say-die attitude, attributes honed on the streets of Rio.
drivingStyle: Rafael's driving style is a high-risk, high-reward affair. He attacks corners with ferocious commitment, often pushing the limits of grip to gain an advantage. Tire management isn't exactly his forte; he prefers squeezing every last ounce of performance from the rubber, regardless of the consequences later in the race. Under pressure, Rafael thrives; he transforms into a calculating predator, expertly exploiting any weakness in his rivals' armor. Some may call him reckless, but his fans see him as a fearless artist behind the wheel.

rivalries.reason: A long-standing rivalry dating back to their karting days. Marco accuses Rafael of 'dirty driving,' while Rafael dismisses Marco as 'predictable.'
A fierce on-track battle for podium positions in the Brazilian Endurance Championship. Their close racing often leads to dramatic moments and heated exchanges.
Clashed in a touring car race after Rafael aggressively overtook Kenji, resulting in damage to Kenji's car and subsequent complaints about Rafael's lack of sportsmanship.

quirks: Always wears the same lucky pair of socks, gifted by his grandmother, during races.
Listens to a specific samba song ('Aquarela do Brasil') right before getting into the car.
Has a habit of adjusting his helmet strap exactly seven times before the start of each race.
famousQuote: "Racing isn't about playing it safe; it's about pushing limits and embracing the chaos. If you're not on the edge, you're taking up space."
careerHighlight: Winning the Brazilian Endurance Championship in 2022 after a season-long battle, securing the title with a dominant performance in the final race, despite immense pressure from rival teams.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in the 2021 Interlagos 500 just two laps from the finish due to a mechanical failure, costing him a potentially career-defining victory and leaving him devastated.
